thread:
tasha: Hey folks — CI is failing in the edge-vitest job when we mock the JS SDK. Local vitest (node env) is fine. Error: "The requested module '/node_modules/@redwood/inference/dist/index.js' does not provide an export named 'createClient'"

ryan: That screams ESM/CJS interop. How are you mocking it?

tasha: Simple mock: `vi.mock('@redwood/inference', () => ({ createClient: vi.fn(() => ({ request: vi.fn() })) }))`. Works locally. CI (edge) fails during module resolution.

anika: Vitest pre-bundles deps for the browser/edge runner and can choose a different entrypoint from package.exports. Check the package.json in node_modules for conditional exports.

tasha: Confirmed. package.json exports map points to dist/index.mjs and dist/index.cjs. The pre-bundler seems to resolve to CJS which changes the runtime shape (default wrapper).

ryan: Quick fixes: 1) force inlining of the SDK in vitest deps: `test: { deps: { inline: ['@redwood/inference'] } }`. 2) Use async mock factory that uses `vi.importActual` to get the correct shape.

nate: If you see the module log as `{ default: { createClient: [Function] } }`, adapt the mock to match that shape: `vi.mock('@redwood/inference', () => ({ default: { createClient: vi.fn() } }))`.

tasha: I tried deps.inline + async factory. Still got `createClient is not a function` until I added a tiny shim in `test/setupTests.ts` that normalizes default -> named: `const m = await import('@redwood/inference'); if (m.default && !m.createClient) Object.assign(m, m.default);` CI passed after that. Gross but effective.

anika: Long-term we should fix SDK packaging so ESM exports are stable (named exports present on the top-level ESM entry) and add a consumer vitest job in the SDK repo to catch regressions.

devops-bot: Created ticket SDK-124: add bundler test and verify package.exports across targets. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/124

ryan: Also add a short note to the JS SDK README showing recommended vitest config and the inline shim workaround for consumers.

tasha: Thanks — I'll open a webapp PR with the shim and link SDK-124. Will follow up to remove shim once SDK packaging is fixed. :thumbsup:
